tables.description: Returns for decile portfolios based on one-dimensional classifications by B/M, C/P, E/P, and GS: R1-R5, AR, CR5, SAAR across 10 deciles, 22 formations April 1968-April 1989.
tables.replication_meaning: Proves the entire core pipeline: NYSE/AMEX universe 1963-1990, 22 annual end-of-April formations, equal-weighted decile sorts on B/M, C/P, E/P and the GS weighted sales-growth rank, annual buy-and-hold R1-R5 with delisted-stock replacement by size-decile returns, CR5 with annual rebalancing, and size-decile-benchmark SAAR. Matching the monotone decile gradients and the glamour-value AR spreads (B/M 10.5pp, C/P 11.0pp, E/P 7.6pp, GS -6.8pp) validates sample construction, variable definitions, and holding-period mechanics at once.
tables.paper_quote: At the end of each April between 1968 and 1989, 10-decile portfolios are formed in ascending order based on B/M, C/P, E/P, and GS. ... AR is the average annual return over 5 postformation years. CR_5 is the compounded 5-year return assuming annual rebalancing. SAAR is the average annual size-adjusted return computed over 5 postformation years.
tables.notes: All 320 paper cells (4 panels x 10 deciles x 8 stats) are targeted except cells with |value| < 0.005 (near-zero SAAR interiors) which are computed and shown in results/table_1.md but not pass/fail scored. GS panel ordering: decile 1 = lowest GS (value), decile 10 = highest GS (glamour).

tables.description: Returns for portfolios based on two-dimensional classifications (30/40/30 independent sorts): C/PxGS, E/PxGS, B/MxGS, E/PxB/M, B/MxC/P; 9 cells each with R1-R5, AR, CR5, SAAR.
tables.replication_meaning: Proves the independent 30/40/30 two-dimensional sort machinery and the glamour/value corner mapping for all five variable pairs - the paper's central contrarian claim that two-dimensional value beats glamour by ~10-11pp/yr (C/PxGS: AR 22.1 vs 11.4; cumulative 171.1 vs 71.2).
tables.paper_quote: The stocks are independently sorted in ascending order into 3 groups (1) bottom 30 percent, (2) middle 40 percent, and (3) top 30 percent) based on each of two variables. ... the value portfolio either refers to the portfolio containing stocks ranked in the top group (3) on both variables from among C/P, E/P, or B/M, or else the portfolio containing stocks ranking in the top group on one of those variables and in the bottom group (1) on GS. The glamour portfolio contains stocks with precisely the opposite set of rankings.
tables.notes: Cell coordinates use the paper's group numbers: (first-var group, second-var group). Glamour corners: A/B/C (1,3); D/E (1,1). Value corners: A/B/C (3,1); D/E (3,3). AR and SAAR value-minus-glamour spreads are added as derived targets (computed from the paper's own cells). Cells with |value| < 0.005 excluded from scoring.

tables.description: Summary version of Table II (AR, CR5, SAAR only) for the subsample of the largest 50 percent of NYSE/AMEX stocks by market capitalization.
tables.replication_meaning: Proves correct large-firm subsample construction (largest 50% of the NYSE/AMEX universe by end-of-April market cap, re-sorted each formation) and validates the robustness claim that the value-glamour spread survives among large caps (C/PxGS SAAR spread 8.7pp, identical to the full sample).
tables.paper_quote: At the end of each April between 1968 and 1989, 9 subgroups of the largest 50 percent of stocks by market capitalization are formed.
tables.notes: Same 9-cell coordinates as Table II. Cells with |value| < 0.005 (several SAAR cells near zero) excluded from scoring.

tables.description: Fama-MacBeth regressions of Year +1 individual stock returns on GS, B/M, SIZE, E/P+, DE/P, C/P+, DC/P: 9 specifications, coefficient means and time-series t-statistics over 22 formations.
tables.replication_meaning: Proves the Fama-MacBeth setup (22 cross-sectional regressions of 1-year stock returns on formation-date characteristics, averaged with time-series t-stats) and validates the variable-significance claim: C/P and GS dominate, B/M's coefficient collapses to ~0 in multiple regressions.
tables.paper_quote: We then run 22 cross-sectional regressions with these returns for each formation period as dependent variables. ... The reported coefficients are averages over the 22 formation periods. The reported t-statistics are based on the time-series variation of the 22 coefficients.
tables.notes: Specifications in paper order: (1) Int+GS, (2) Int+B/M, (3) Int+SIZE, (4) Int+E/P+, (5) Int+C/P+, (6) Int+GS+B/M+C/P++DC/P, (7) Int+B/M+SIZE+C/P++DC/P, (8) Int+GS+B/M+SIZE+C/P++DC/P, (9) Int+GS+B/M+SIZE+E/P++DE/P. Regression runs over ALL sample firms (including negative E/P, C/P firms via the dummy construction).

tables.description: Fundamental variables (E/P, C/P, S/P, D/P, B/M, SIZE), past growth (-5,0), and future growth (0,5),(2,5) for glamour vs value portfolios under the B/M decile and C/PxGS classifications.
tables.replication_meaning: Proves the accounting-growth machinery: per-$1-invested portfolio fundamentals and the paper's unusual growth-rate convention (per-dollar fundamentals summed within each formation year, then averaged across the 22 formations before differencing). Validates the extrapolation mechanism: glamour's high past growth does not persist post-formation.
tables.paper_quote: E/P, C/P, S/P, D/P, B/M, and SIZE, defined below, use the end-of-April market value of equity and preformation year accounting numbers. ... AEG_(i,j) is the geometric average growth rate of earnings for the portfolio from year i to year j. ACG_(i,j) and ASG_(i,j) are defined analogously for cash flow and sales, respectively. RETURN_(-3,0) is the cumulative stock return on the portfolio over the 3 years prior to formation.
tables.notes: Glamour/value definitions: Panel 1 = B/M deciles 1 vs 10; Panel 2 = (CP1,GS3) vs (CP3,GS1). S/P and D/P rows are part of the same parsed table. SIZE is in millions of dollars.

tables.description: Year-by-year value-minus-glamour returns over 1-, 3-, and 5-year holding horizons for each April 1968-1989 formation, for C/P deciles (9,10 vs 1,2), C/PxGS corners, and B/M deciles (10,9 vs 1,2); with arithmetic means and Hansen-Hodrick t-statistics.
tables.replication_meaning: Proves overlapping multi-year buy-and-hold spread construction per formation year and the Hansen-Hodrick MA(2)/MA(4) standard errors; validates the consistency claim (value beats glamour in 17-19 of 22 one-year windows and in every 5-year window).
tables.paper_quote: We consider differences in cumulative returns between deciles (9, 10) and (1, 2) for C/P and B/M, and between groups (3, 1) and (1, 3) for (C/P, GS) over 1-, 3-, and 5-year holding horizons starting each year in the sample (1968, 1969, etc.). ... Standard errors for t-tests involving overlapping 3- and 5-year horizons are computed using the method of Hansen-Hodrick (1980), assuming annual MA(2) and MA(4) processes, respectively.
tables.notes: Panel 2's C/PxGS spread uses value (CP3,GS1) minus glamour (CP1,GS3) per the paper caption. Later formations have blank 3-/5-year cells (insufficient post-sample data) and are skipped. Year cells with |value| < 0.005 skipped.

tables.description: Average monthly portfolio returns across four market states (W25 worst, N88 other negative, P122 other positive, B25 best months by the EW index): Panel 1A C/PxGS 9 portfolios + index; Panel 1B B/M deciles + index, spread, t-stat.
tables.replication_meaning: Proves monthly attribution of annually-rebalanced portfolios (portfolio membership changes every April) to EW-index market states, and validates the no-downside-risk claim: value loses less than glamour in the worst 25 months (C/PxGS: -8.6% vs -10.3%; B/M: spread +1.1pp, t=1.8).
tables.paper_quote: All months in the sample are divided into 25 worst stock return months based on the equally weighted index (W_25), the remaining 88 negative months other than the 25 worst (N_88), the 122 positive months other than the 25 best (P_122), and the 25 best months (B_25) in the sample. ... For each portfolio (changing every April), Panel 1A presents its average return over the W_25, N_88, P_122, and B_25 months.
tables.notes: OUT OF SCOPE: Panel 2A/2B (GNP-growth-quarter states) require quarterly real GNP data (BEA) not present in ClickHouse; Panel 1 is the paper's primary downside-risk test and Panel 2 'mirrors the basic conclusions from Panel 1' (paper p. 1568). Panel 1A Value-Glamour spread and t columns are not targeted because the OCR'd column alignment is ambiguous; the pinned glamour (CP1,GS3) and value (CP3,GS1) cells ARE targeted and match the paper's prose (p. 1567: W25 value -8.6%, glamour -10.3%; N88 value -1.5%, glamour -2.9%, index -2.3%). Month states run May 1968 - April 1995 (months covered by annually-held portfolios).

tables.description: Traditional risk measures from the 22 year-after-formation return observations per portfolio: beta vs the value-weighted index, standard deviation of returns, standard deviation of size-adjusted returns. Panel 1: C/P deciles; Panel 2: C/PxGS groups; Panel 3: B/M deciles.
tables.replication_meaning: Proves the 22-observation annual return series per portfolio and CAPM beta vs the VW index, and validates the traditional-risk claim: value betas only ~0.1 higher than glamour, and size-adjusted return volatility is nearly identical - risk cannot explain the 10-11pp return spread.
tables.paper_quote: For each portfolio described below, we compute, using 22 year-after-the-formation returns as observations, its beta with respect to the value-weighted index. Using the 22 formation periods, we also compute the standard deviation of returns and the standard deviation of size-adjusted returns in the year after formation.
tables.notes: Known OCR limitations: Panel 2 columns are corrupted - the OCR dropped/misordered portfolio columns and the paper's prose (p. 1569: value std 24.1% vs glamour 21.6%) is inconsistent with every mapping of the six visible cells, so Panel 2 portfolio cells are NOT scored; only its EW-index column (identity-pinned: beta 1.304, std 0.250, matching Panel 1's EW index) is targeted. The replication computes all 9 Panel 2 portfolios and reports them unscored in results/table_8.md. Panel 3 shows only B/M deciles 1-6 (OCR truncated deciles 7-10). Beta uses excess returns over the risk-free rate (ff.four_factor_monthly.rf) vs the VW index per paper L2342.
